text:
Maya: quick heads-up — starting staged v2 rollout to prod in 15m (15:00 UTC). this deploy includes the header normalization change (X-Client-Version). tagging mobile + eu first. any last-minute compatibility concerns?

deploy-bot: Scheduled rollout: v2 -> api-gateway. canary targets: mobile, eu-region, 5% traffic. window: 15:00-16:00 UTC. ops runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/v2-rollout

Sahil: saw a small spike on the eu test cluster during the internal canary earlier — roughly 2% increased 5xx for routes with legacy clients (no X-Client-Version). not sure if it's from header parsing or a downstream assumption. leaving dashboards open.

Jorge: noted. on v1 the gateway accepted header-absent requests. v2 treats missing header as "unknown" and some downstreams interpret that as auth mismatch. quick fix = gateway fallback shim that maps missing header -> "legacy". can we inject that without re-deploying the model servers?

Liz: +1 for shim. if we can toggle it at the gateway layer we should. otherwise we need a temporary pin to v1 for mobile routes. pinging is low-risk and reversible.

Maya: deploy-bot, can we hold canary and apply a shim toggle? i don't want to push full rollout if mobile clients are at risk.

deploy-bot: Canary paused by operator request (Maya). Reason: compatibility check. Current canary traffic frozen at 5%. To resume, run `/deploy resume 2439991234` or apply toggle via config.

Sahil: quick telemetry check — user agents show ~18% of mobile traffic doesn't send X-Client-Version. that's higher than expected. suggestion: pin mobile route back to v1 while we roll out shim and notify SDK teams.

Jorge: agree. propose actions in order: 1) pin /v2/mobile -> v1 (traffic routing) 2) enable gateway header-fallback shim 3) update release notes + notify SDK oncall 4) resume canary at 2% for 1h then step up.

Ashley: i'll take release notes and comms. will add a note about header behavior and call out the SDK upgrade. draft: "v2 normalizes client header X-Client-Version; servers will route unknown -> legacy if shim not enabled. Mobile SDKs < 3.2 may omit header — pinning applied to avoid disruption."

Maya: approved. let's run pin + shim. command i'll execute: 
```
# pin mobile route to v1
deploy routing apply --route "/v2/mobile" --pin-version v1 --reason "header-compatibility pause"
# enable gateway fallback
gateway-config set header_fallback.enabled true --env prod --note "temporary shim for missing X-Client-Version"
```

deploy-bot: Action: routing pin applied by Maya at 15:07 UTC. /v2/mobile -> v1 pinned. Action: gateway header_fallback.enabled = true by Maya at 15:08 UTC.

Liz: confirming mobile error rate dropped to baseline in EU after pin + shim. nice work. logs show older clients now get legacy mapping.

Sahil: rolling metrics look good. no increase in downstream auth errors. recommend holding canary for 1h at 2% and then progress.

Jorge: will prepare a quick revert playbook in case we see auth regressions after resume. include steps: `deploy routing rollback --route "/v2/mobile" --to-unpinned` and `gateway-config set header_fallback.enabled false` plus alerting thresholds.

Maya: thanks all — Ashley please send release note + notify SDK slack. i'll resume canary at 16:15 UTC once comms are out and we have 1h of stable metrics. :thumbsup:

Ashley: Will post notes and ping SDK oncall now. Draft posted: https://internal.redwood/notes/v2-header-compat. tagging #sdk-updates. :loud_sound:

deploy-bot: Resume scheduled: /deploy resume 2439991234 by Maya at 16:15 UTC (waiting). If any operator reacts with :no_entry: before resume, deploy will remain paused.

Maya: leaving this thread open for post-rollout signals. if anything spikes, call the rollback steps in Jorge's playbook.

Liz: quick follow — Ops reminder: add a short-term dashboard tile for percent of requests missing X-Client-Version, do we have an existing metric? if not, i'll add a synthetic from the gateway logs.

Sahil: we have it under gateway.metrics.request_headers.missing_x_client_version. i'll add alert: >5% for 10m triggers page to oncall.

Maya: perfect. closing the loop once canary completes. thanks everyone.
